clue.text: You may see this as an orchestra, too

parts.note: the indefinite article as a single letter
the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A musing that something might be viewed as an orchestra as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites you to read the four-letter answer as 'A LSO', that is, an orchestra; the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are adverbial synonyms, both meaning in addition.

clue.text: Lucerne footballers welcomed by all footballers

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by hosts is taken in among them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written; it wraps the first footballers
the Football Association, inside the word all
the Football Association again, added at the end

explanation.surface: A team from the Swiss city of Lucerne is greeted by every footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucerne looks like the Swiss city, but it is also a name for a fodder plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the usual British name for the forage crop that Americans call alfalfa.

clue.text: Stop assuming decline in recycling is an economic problem

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the first word takes the rest inside itself

parts.note: a stop on a railway line

indicators.note: something being recycled is broken down and remade in a fresh form

parts.note: to flag is to weaken or decline

explanation.surface: Ending the assumption that recycling is falling off would be an economic worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagflation is the combination of stagnant growth and rising inflation that troubles economies.

clue.text: Threw mud? Mud had to be thrown

indicators.note: letters that are thrown get scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: all ten letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether mud was flung, and is told it simply had to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threw mud' is figurative: to sling mud is to speak ill of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing mud means making damaging remarks, which is exactly what criticising someone spitefully involves.

clue.text: Complete authority needs no introduction

indicators.note: the word must go without its introduction, meaning its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a warrant is an official authority to act

explanation.surface: Total power that is so well known it needs no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant is an intensifier meaning utter or out-and-out, as in arrant nonsense.

clue.text: Cloth skirts on trial

parts.note: minis are short skirts
a try is an attempt or trial

explanation.surface: Fabric used to make skirts is being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is a traditional term for the clergy, so Cloth is not fabric here.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministry and the cloth both refer to the body of clergy and their profession.

clue.text: Set Sunday Times cryptic out of order

indicators.note: a cryptic version is obscured and disguised, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: all fourteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A complaint that the paper's set crossword is jumbled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: the puzzle's own name supplies every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsystematised lacks method or arrangement, so it is disorganised, in no proper order.

clue.text: The man carrying old gardening tool

indicators.note: a person carrying something holds it within, so one part wraps another

parts.note: the male pronoun
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A man carrying an antique implement for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled garden implement for weeding and loosening soil.

clue.text: Indecisive jockeys try and hide

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and jostle for position, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Riders who can't make up their minds attempt to conceal themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone who dithers, wavering and unable to make up their mind.

clue.text: A 4×4's turn in the car's role — looking ridiculous

indicators.note: one element goes inside the other once that has been rearranged
something made to look ridiculous is distorted out of its proper shape

parts.note: the anagram fodder, rearranged to wrap the next piece
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: A sports utility vehicle plays its part in a film, appearing absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea tractor is British slang mocking big off-road cars driven in wealthy parts of London such as Chelsea; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a derisive nickname for a four-wheel-drive SUV used only on city streets.

clue.text: Take advantage of down payments?

parts.note: surface reading: exploit a deposit scheme or instalment plan; setter's reading: down means soft plumage, the material a bird lines its home with

explanation.walkthrough: Down payments sounds financial; read down as soft plumage and the idiom for enriching yourself, typically by abusing a position, appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to enrich oneself, often dishonestly, by profiting from one's position.

clue.text: May 23, these 50 cats will cuddle one

definitions.note: a phrase pointing at the answer: these may come to the rescue (23 across)

indicators.note: things that cuddle something hold it between them, enclosing it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
felines are cats
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A note that on May 23rd fifty cats will snuggle up with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: May 23 looks like a date; it means 'may' plus the answer to 23 across, COME TO THE RESCUE. The I sits between the L and the cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifelines are ropes or means of support thrown to people in trouble, so they can save them.

clue.text: Border around left edge

indicators.note: around places one element so it surrounds another

parts.note: a side is a border or boundary
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A frontier line running around the outermost left-hand rim.
explanation.walkthrough: Edge looks like a noun matching border, but it is the verb, meaning move gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move furtively sideways, much as one edges along a wall.

clue.text: Theatre part for Garbo?

parts.note: surface reading: a section of the auditorium reserved for the film star Greta Garbo; setter's reading: split Garbo as GARB plus O, clothing and a ring, which is what the two words of the theatre area mean

explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer's two words, taken as clothing plus a ring, would clue GARB O. The name points to the actress, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first balcony of seats above the stalls in a theatre, once requiring evening wear.

clue.text: The morning crossword in a Sunday paper was stunning

parts.note: abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon
Azed is the long-running cryptic puzzle in The Observer, a British Sunday paper

explanation.surface: Someone praises the morning's puzzle in a weekend newspaper as superb.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed is the pseudonym of the Observer's barred-grid crossword, named after Torquemada of the Inquisition, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: If something amazed, it astonished people, much as anything stunning dazzles those who see it.

clue.text: Author, given lines, leaves

parts.note: Graham Greene, the English novelist
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A writer, handed some lines, walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like a verb, departs, but it is the plural noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage or vegetation, a collective term for plants' leaves.

clue.text: Make a boob? Don't worry

parts.note: to forge is to make or shape
boob and tit are both slang for a breast

explanation.surface: Someone asks about committing a blunder and is told not to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: Make a boob sounds like make a mistake; instead boob is read as a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic way to dismiss something, telling someone to stop bothering about it.

clue.text: Piano is not TV studio equipment

parts.note: musical notation for softly
informal contraction
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A piano isn't a piece of gear for a television studio.
explanation.walkthrough: TV studio reads as a phrase, but TV belongs to the wordplay and the studio is an artist's.
explanation.definitionFit: A paintbox holds an artist's set of colours, the kind of kit found in a painter's studio.

clue.text: Sweep with long flourish

parts.note: a camera pans as it sweeps across a scene
to ache for is to long for

explanation.surface: A broad brushstroke made with an extended decorative twirl.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is stylish verve and dash, a showy flamboyance of manner.

clue.text: Officer hiding behind one lieutenant

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it concealed inside itself

parts.note: commanding officer
slang for the backside
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A military officer lurks at the back of a single junior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello, Cassio is promoted as the general's lieutenant, which sparks Iago's jealousy.

clue.text: Friend using jagged blade to cut leg

indicators.note: to cut into something is to enter it, so one piece lands within another

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: something jagged is broken and uneven, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pal wields a serrated knife to slice into a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is a dated, jovial British form of address for a friend or chap.

clue.text: Very rainy over some of Johannesburg

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
wet weather is rainy
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Heavy rainfall falling over part of a South African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Some of looks like a signal to take letters from Johannesburg; it is the definition, a part of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is a large township forming part of the city of Johannesburg in South Africa.

clue.text: Saucy writer starts to joke about assassin

parts.note: Anaïs Nin, famous for erotic writing

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A racy author begins to make jokes about a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealth and used as a spy or hired killer.

clue.text: "Good Lord" goes around if that is given worship

indicators.note: one part going around others encloses them within itself

parts.note: standard abbreviation for good
taken as written; it wraps what follows
taken as written
abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise spreads when a deity is adored.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify is to praise or exalt, so something glorified has been honoured with worship.

clue.text: Wake up — there's a suggestion to be a hero

parts.note: to come to is to regain consciousness
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a cue is a hint or prompt

explanation.surface: A rallying call: rouse yourself, here is an idea for being brave.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls in the middle of a word: the clue's there's plus a hint run together as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to someone's rescue means saving them, the archetypal heroic act.

clue.text: Plan starters of meat and potatoes

indicators.note: starters are what comes first, so each word yields its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Planning the first courses of a meat-and-potatoes meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan can be a drawing or chart of an area, the same sense as a map.

clue.text: Atonement's right in the end

indicators.note: one element is placed in another

parts.note: expiation is atonement; the 's means has
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Making amends is justified when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: In the end reads as a phrase meaning ultimately, but in is the insertion signal and the end the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Expiration means expiry or termination, a coming to a close.

clue.text: Poor or very good

definitions.meaning: slang for excellent, as in a cook who makes a terrific curry

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings contradict each other, which makes the clue look impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective can mean shabby and inferior, yet informally also means excellent or skilful.
